notes.summary: One-word substitution asks for the single word that means the same as a group of words (one who collects stamps = philatelist). SSC asks 1 to 2 such questions in Tier 1 and more in Tier 2. The words fall into a few families: people, sciences, governments and beliefs, killings and fears, places, qualities, actions, and things. Knowing a handful of roots (-cide, -phobia, -cracy, -logy, -vore) lets you work out many answers.

concepts.title: How SSC asks and how to solve
concepts.body:
• Usual form: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Willful destruction. Answer: sabotage.
  • In a sentence: Rohan is the one who opposes others. Answer: antagonist.
  1. Find the key idea (stamps, heights, king, cannot be read).
  2. Find the family: person (-ist, -er), study (-logy), killing (-cide), fear (-phobia), rule (-cracy), quality (in-...-ible).
  3. Check the part of speech. That which cannot be read needs an adjective (illegible); to increase speed needs a verb (accelerate).
  4. Eliminate look-alikes: illegible (cannot be read) vs ineligible (not qualified).

varieties.name: Words for people
varieties.how: Find the habit, belief, job or age being described, then recall the matching -ist, -er or -arian word.

example.q:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute.
A person whose age is between 70 and 79 years
steps: Age words: sexa- (60s), septua- (70s), octo- (80s), nona- (90s).
Only one names the exact decade.

varieties.name: Study of something (-logy and sciences)
varieties.how: Spot the subject of study and add the Greek or Latin root: ornitho (bird), entomo (insect), seismo (earthquake), derma (skin).

example.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
The study of insects
steps: Options: Etymology (word origins), Entomology, Ornithology (birds), Zoology (animals).

varieties.name: Government and beliefs (-cracy, -archy, -ism)
varieties.how: For rule, find who holds power (wealthy, few, priests, officials) and match the -cracy or -archy word. For beliefs, match the -ism.

example.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
Government by the wealthy
steps: Options: Autocracy (one ruler), Bureaucracy (officials), Plutocracy, Aristocracy (nobles).

varieties.name: Killing, fears and manias
varieties.how: Killing → -cide, fear → -phobia, urge → -mania. Then match the victim or object: regi (king), fratri (brother), acro (height), claustro (closed space).

example.q:
Select the one-word substitute.
Killing of one's brother

varieties.name: Places and collections
varieties.how: Identify what is kept or gathered (bees, birds, weapons, poems), then recall the place or collection word.

example.q:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.
An arrangement of flowers that is usually given as a present
steps: A garland is worn; a wreath is a ring of flowers, often for funerals; a bundle is not specific to flowers.
A bouquet is a bunch of flowers given as a present.

varieties.name: Qualities (that which cannot be…)
varieties.how: The answer is an adjective, usually in-/im-/il-/ir- + root + -ible/-able. Match the root to the verb: legere (read), audire (hear), vincere (conquer).

example.q:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.
That which cannot be satisfied

varieties.name: Actions (verbs)
varieties.how: A description starting with To… needs a verb. Pick the verb whose meaning matches exactly, not a related noun or adjective.

example.q:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.
To increase the speed
steps: Options: Accelerate, Assimilate (absorb), Activate (start), Exhilarate (make very happy).

varieties.name: Things, writings and events
varieties.how: Decide what kind of thing it is (list, speech, writing, act, remedy) and recall the exact noun. Eliminate near meanings.

example.q:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute.
Wilful destruction
steps: A disaster or calamity is not deliberate; combustion is burning.

varieties.name: One word for a phrase in a sentence
varieties.how: Turn the underlined phrase into a stand-alone description, find the word, then check it fits the sentence grammatically.

example.q:
Select the one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.
Out of those group members, Rohan is the one who opposes others, no matter what they tell him.
steps: A protagonist is the main character or a supporter; an antagonist opposes.

tips: Find the family first: person, study, rule, killing, fear, place, quality, action or thing.
Check the part of speech the description needs: That which cannot be… gives an adjective, To… gives a verb.
Age words go by decade: septuagenarian (70s), octogenarian (80s), nonagenarian (90s).
Revise the one-word flashcards in themes; SSC repeats many words year after year.
Use elimination: the wrong options are usually words from the same family.
traps: Emigrant leaves a country; immigrant comes into one.
Astronomy is the science of stars; astrology claims they shape human lives.
Antagonist opposes; protagonist is the main character or a supporter.
Bouquet is given as a present; wreath is a ring of flowers, often for funerals; garland is worn.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
The study of birds
questions.solution: ornith = bird, -logy = study. Ornithology. Entomology = insects; Anthropology = humans.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
A person who loves mankind and works for its welfare
questions.solution: phil = love, anthropos = man. Philanthropist. A misanthrope hates mankind; a philatelist collects stamps.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
That which cannot be read
questions.solution: Illegible = cannot be read (of handwriting). Ineligible = not qualified; inaudible = cannot be heard.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
Government by the wealthy
questions.solution: plutos = wealth, -cracy = rule. Plutocracy. Aristocracy = rule by nobles; autocracy = rule by one person.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
A person who is unable to be corrected or reformed
questions.solution: Incorrigible = cannot be corrected. Invincible = cannot be defeated; indefatigable = never tired; inexorable = cannot be stopped or persuaded.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
questions.solution: Agenda = list of items to be discussed at a meeting. Inventory = list of goods in stock; manifesto = public declaration of policy.
